meeting_header: Date: 2026-12-20 15:30 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Lucas Ortega (Redwood SE); Priya Nair (Redwood CSM); Daniel Park (Pavo CTO); Sana Malik (Pavo ML); Omar Reyes (Pavo DevOps)
summary: Discovery/POC scoping call to agree pilot success criteria, workload sizing and benchmarks for an OpenAI-compatible integration. Discussed SDK vs raw endpoints, function/tool calling with structured JSON output, security (VPC, SOC2, KMS), and a two-week pilot timeline with explicit benchmark metrics (latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, cost). Agreed next steps and owners.
topics: Benchmarks: tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, fallback behaviours
Integration: SDKs vs OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function/tool calling
Security & networking: VPC peering, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we're going to run through the scope for the POC — goal is to make sure the integration path and benchmarks are clear. um, quick intros?
[00:10] Daniel Park: hi, daniel here, cto at pavo. we'll be owner on the infra side.
[00:14] Sana Malik: sana, lead ml eng. i'll own model and prompts.
[00:18] Omar Reyes: omar, devops. i'll handle networking and security.
[00:21] Lucas Ortega: lucas from redwood, se focused on benchmarks and infra.
[00:24] Maya Chen: great. agenda is success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, and integration approach — sdk vs openai-style endpoints and tool calling. sound good?
[00:30] Daniel Park: yes. quick context: our main product uses a chat assistant + integrated tools for db queries and a billing lookup. roughly 1200 concurrent active users at peak, but only ~140 qps when aggregated because sessions are multi-turn.
[00:44] Sana Malik: workload mix is ~60% short chat responses (<100 tokens), 30% medium summaries (200-600 tokens), 10% tool-calling flows that may include multiple turns and structured JSON outputs.
[00:56] Maya Chen: good, that's helpful. for success criteria, what would you consider a pass?
[01:01] Daniel Park: latency is big. p50 under 250ms and p95 below 800ms for the short chat bucket is our target. for tool flows, p95 can be higher but we'd like sub-2s ideally.
[01:14] Sana Malik: also cost: we have a budget to keep cost per 1M tokens under a certain threshold — i'll share numbers, but we want to see redwood beat what we're currently paying on the managed endpoint.
[01:25] Lucas Ortega: makes sense. for the pilot we usually measure p50/p95, tokens per second, and cost per 1M tokens given the quantization profile. we'll capture quality regressions via your eval prompt set.
[01:36] Maya Chen: can you confirm data residency or compliance needs? SOC2 or ISO?
[01:41] Omar Reyes: we need SOC2 and enterprise audit logs; flexible key management is preferred — we'll want KMS integration for private deployments but for pilot hosted is fine if logs are retained and encrypted.
[01:53] Maya Chen: Redwood supports SOC2 and KMS integrations on Private; for hosted pilot we can provide tenant-level encryption and audit logs, and for Dedicated/Private we can add customer-managed KMS.
[02:04] Sana Malik: on the integration side, we prefer OpenAI-compatible endpoints so minimal code changes. do you have full parity on function calling and structured output?
[02:12] Lucas Ortega: yes, we support OpenAI-style REST endpoints and SDKs. function/tool calling is supported and we have structured output helpers — we validate JSON schema at the runtime if you enable structured-output mode. small caveat: there are occasional differences in tokenization and streaming edge cases, we’ll call those out in the benchmark reports.
[02:29] Daniel Park: streaming edge cases? can you give an example?
[02:31] Lucas Ortega: sometimes when streaming plus schema enforcement, you see truncated streams if the model tries to emit more tokens than the schema allows; our runtime will surface a schema-violation error and optionally emit partial payloads. we'll include that in validation.
[02:44] Maya Chen: ok practical plan — we propose a two-week pilot: week 1 onboarding, run benchmarks, week 2 iterate on config (batching, kv cache, quantization). is that feasible?
[02:56] Omar Reyes: timeline sounds tight but doable. i'll need to open firewall rules and do VPC peering, which may take 48 hours.
[03:02] Daniel Park: we can prioritize the short-chat trace first to get early latency numbers.
[03:06] Sana Malik: i'll prepare a 50-prompt eval set and 3 workload traces: short-chat, long summarization, and tool-calling flow.
[03:12] Maya Chen: perfect. benchmark specifics: we'll run 3 kinds of tests — steady-state throughput for tokens/sec, latency distribution for each bucket, and a mixed-volume stress test to exercise autoscaling and fallback.
[03:25] Lucas Ortega: and we'll test both: OpenAI-compatible endpoints (so you can drop-in) and our SDK which provides auto-batching and improved KV cache handling out of the box. SDK tends to reduce p95 by 10-30% in our internal tests for small chat latencies.
[03:38] Daniel Park: what does the SDK add?
[03:40] Lucas Ortega: it abstracts batching, streaming semantics, and integrates the KV cache for multi-turn — you get continuous batching and smarter kernel selection. if you go raw endpoint you get simpler request patterns but you'll need to implement batching client-side for best cost/latency.
[03:53] Sana Malik: function calling — our flows encode a SQL-like query tool and a billing lookup tool. we need deterministic JSON schema for the tool outputs. can you enforce schema and fail the call if schema mismatch?
[04:05] Lucas Ortega: yes we can enable strict schema enforcement. the runtime can return a structured error and optionally fallback to a recovery model if enabled.
[04:12] Maya Chen: also want to call out caching — prefix/KV caching will reduce token cost if you have repeated contexts. if your app has repeated system prompts or doc contexts, it can materially lower cost.
[04:24] Daniel Park: we do have repeated prompts across sessions, especially for onboarding flows. how much savings is typical?
[04:29] Lucas Ortega: depends, but we see 20-40% token reduction in workloads with repeated prefixes. we'll include a cache-effectiveness metric in the benchmark.
[04:36] Omar Reyes: on security, what's needed for the hosted pilot? we prefer VPC peering for test infra, otherwise at minimum IP allowlist.
[04:44] Maya Chen: we can do either. VPC peering for Private/Dedicated, for hosted pilot we usually do VPN/IP allowlist and mutual TLS if desired. we'll email the exact checklist.
[04:54] Sana Malik: measuring 'quality'—we want to avoid hallucinations in tool outputs. are you able to run automated evals against a ground-truth set?
[05:01] Lucas Ortega: yes, provide ground-truth and we run the eval harness that measures exact-match, F1, and schema-validity for structured outputs. we'll flag regressions relative to a baseline model.
[05:10] Daniel Park: baseline is our current managed model (we'll include baseline metrics).
[05:14] Maya Chen: great. pilot acceptance criteria proposal: 1) short-chat p50 < 250ms and p95 < 800ms, 2) structured-tool flows schema-validity > 98% on the eval set, 3) cost per 1M tokens lower than baseline by at least 15% or same cost with 20% better latency. agree?
[05:29] Sana Malik: that sounds reasonable. can we add an availability SLA during pilot? maybe 99.5%?
[05:35] Priya Nair: (Redwood CSM) we can commit to monitoring and an interim uptime target for the pilot and include incident reporting - full SLA is for Dedicated/Private contracts.
[05:45] Omar Reyes: any limits on model versions? we want to test one of the open models you validated and a quantized variant.
[05:52] Lucas Ortega: yes we can run both a full and an int8 quantized build. we'll include performance delta and quality delta.
[06:00] Daniel Park: benchmarking mechanics — we want the run to be reproducible. will you provide the benchmark harness or do we run on our side?
[06:06] Lucas Ortega: Redwood will provide a benchmark harness and scripts, but we can also run on your infra if you prefer. typical is Redwood runs controlled jobs against your account endpoints and we share raw logs and dashboards.
[06:18] Maya Chen: as for data flows — logs are retained and we can redact user PII. we will set retention based on your needs.
[06:25] Omar Reyes: KMS integration for Dedicated — if we transition after pilot, what's the migration story?
[06:30] Lucas Ortega: migration is straightforward — we can rekey datasets and enable customer-managed keys in the private control plane; we have runbooks for that.
[06:37] Daniel Park: pricing — maya, can you outline pilot pricing vs committed Dedicated pricing?
[06:40] Maya Chen: yes i'll send the SOW and a pilot price sheet. pilots are usage-based with a small onboarding fee; Dedicated discounts kick in at monthly commit tiers.
[06:49] Sana Malik: curious about autoscaling behavior in sudden spikes — we need graceful degradation and fallback to smaller cheaper models.
[06:56] Lucas Ortega: smart routing supports tiered fallbacks: we can route to a cheaper quantized variant or to a regional fallback. you can configure strictness — whether to prefer latency or cost.
[07:07] Maya Chen: we'll include a recommended routing policy for your traffic profile.
[07:11] Daniel Park: any gotchas with tool calling and streaming? like ordering guarantees?
[07:16] Lucas Ortega: streaming with tool calling is supported, but ordering is eventual if you use parallel tool calls. serialized tool calls keep order but may increase latency. we'll show tradeoffs in the benchmark.
[07:29] Omar Reyes: about VPC peering/test connectivity — I need the IP ranges and peering doc to open firewall rules.
[07:34] Maya Chen: i'll add that to the onboarding checklist.
[07:37] Priya Nair: recap — we'll send SOW, bench runbook, and onboarding checklist. Customer supplies workload traces and eval sets. SE will schedule the benchmark window.
[07:48] Daniel Park: for the benchmark window, we prefer mornings pacific, week of 12/29.
[07:52] Lucas Ortega: noted, i'll propose two slots and we can pick one.
[07:55] Sana Malik: small question — SDK language support? we use nodejs and python.
[07:59] Lucas Ortega: official SDKs in python and node, with examples for streaming and function calling. we'll share sample code for your flow.
[08:07] Daniel Park: any compliance docs we can review? SOC2 report, encryption whitepaper?
[08:11] Maya Chen: yes we'll attach SOC2 attest, architecture whitepaper, and the private deployment security checklist.
[08:18] Omar Reyes: last nit — logging, can we push logs to our splunk or S3?
[08:22] Maya Chen: audit logs can be shipped via secure forwarder to S3 or to SIEMs; we'll include options in the checklist.
[08:29] Daniel Park: ok i think we have enough to start.
[08:31] Maya Chen: great. quick recap of owners and dates. Maya sends SOW and IP checklist by 12/22. Sana to share traces 12/24. Omar to share networking details 12/23. Lucas to prep runbook by 12/28 and run benchmarks in week of 12/29.
[08:48] Sana Malik: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:50] Maya Chen: thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.
[08:53] Daniel Park: thanks. bye.
[08:55] (call ends)

Notes: transcript includes minor mis-transcriptions (e.g., 'kv cache' heard as 'k v cash' occasionally) and occasional speaker label ambiguity in a few lines. SE will attach the benchmark config and sample SDK snippets in follow-up email.
file_notes: Pilot focuses on OpenAI-compatible integration and structured output validation; use SDK for best latency; pilot SOW + bench runbook to be delivered.
